+# Quota Park Probe
+
+Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded probe count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).
+
+Probe success means the quota window has reset or the provider was reconfigured — the handler removes the park label, clears the development/rework dispatch trigger labels, moves the ticket back to Ready For Development and posts an un-park comment, so the normal dispatch lanes resume on the next tick. Probe failure keeps the park and posts a one-line `quota-probe: <n>` marker comment that doubles as the durable counter for the next tick's cadence decision.
+
+## Parameters
+
+- `jobParams.quotaParkLabel` — park label name to watch and remove (default `provider_quota`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = provider_quota`) must be overridden to match.

+
+A human un-parks immediately by removing the park label from the ticket — the probe rule stops matching and no further probes fire.

# gh-1087: [GOAL] Quota circuit-breaker: provider-quota exhaustion (403 usage-limit) parks the lane instead of per-tick retry burn (live: fa gh-1697 loop risk)

## Description

## Goal — provider-quota exhaustion parks the leg lane instead of per-tick retry burn (v1)

One sentence: **a hard provider-quota failure (403 weekly/usage-limit, not transient 429) parks the ticket's leg lane with a visible label and a reason comment** — retries resume only after the quota window resets or a human reconfigures the provider — instead of resetting the ticket for an immediate retry that is guaranteed to fail again.

Live: fa gh-1697, 2026-10-19 06:31–06:33Z — z.ai `glm-5.3-flash` answered 403 "weekly (7-day) usage limit" (9 retries), the whole provider chain exhausted, fa exited 1, gh-742 reset the ticket to Ready For Development. The next SM tick re-dispatches the same leg into the same exhausted chain — a burn loop measured in runner-minutes and noise comments until the 7-day window resets.

## Root cause

The interruption classifier treats a quota-exhausted chain the same as a transient interruption (rate limit blip, network cut). Transients deserve immediate retry; a 7-day quota wall does not. The signal is distinguishable: HTTP 403 with a usage-limit body vs 429 rate-limit.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC3** — The park self-lifts when a bounded probe (one cheap provider ping per N ticks, not a full leg) succeeds — or a human removes the label. Probe cadence and the label name are config (`jobParams`), defaults sane.
- **AC4** — Transient interruptions keep today's gh-742 behavior exactly (reset + retry) — regression guard.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — classifier: 403-weekly-limit → quota_exhausted; 429 → transient; mixed chain ending in quota → quota_exhausted (AC1).
- `UT-2` — park path: label + comment + no status reset (AC2); probe-success un-park (AC3).
- `REG-1` — gh-742 reset-path tests unchanged on transient fixtures (AC4).

## Non-goals

- Provider failover config (the chain already exists and was exhausted — this card governs the aftermath, not provider selection).
- Cross-repo quota accounting.

# gh-1087: [GOAL] Quota circuit-breaker: provider-quota exhaustion (403 usage-limit) parks the lane instead of per-tick retry burn (live: fa gh-1697 loop risk)

## Description

## Goal — provider-quota exhaustion parks the leg lane instead of per-tick retry burn (v1)

One sentence: **a hard provider-quota failure (403 weekly/usage-limit, not transient 429) parks the ticket's leg lane with a visible label and a reason comment** — retries resume only after the quota window resets or a human reconfigures the provider — instead of resetting the ticket for an immediate retry that is guaranteed to fail again.

Live: fa gh-1697, 2026-10-19 06:31–06:33Z — z.ai `glm-5.3-flash` answered 403 "weekly (7-day) usage limit" (9 retries), the whole provider chain exhausted, fa exited 1, gh-742 reset the ticket to Ready For Development. The next SM tick re-dispatches the same leg into the same exhausted chain — a burn loop measured in runner-minutes and noise comments until the 7-day window resets.

## Root cause

The interruption classifier treats a quota-exhausted chain the same as a transient interruption (rate limit blip, network cut). Transients deserve immediate retry; a 7-day quota wall does not. The signal is distinguishable: HTTP 403 with a usage-limit body vs 429 rate-limit.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The leg's agent-failure classification distinguishes `quota_exhausted` (403 usage-limit / billing bodies, "Provider chain exhausted" after quota responses) from `transient` (429, timeouts, cuts). Fixture-driven unit test on the classifier.
- **AC2** — On `quota_exhausted`: the ticket is NOT reset to Ready For Development; instead it (and the PR if present) gets a park label (e.g. `provider_quota`) with a comment naming the provider, the quota window text, and the reset condition. The SM excludes the label from dispatch lanes.
- **AC3** — The park self-lifts when a bounded probe (one cheap provider ping per N ticks, not a full leg) succeeds — or a human removes the label. Probe cadence and the label name are config (`jobParams`), defaults sane.
- **AC4** — Transient interruptions keep today's gh-742 behavior exactly (reset + retry) — regression guard.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — classifier: 403-weekly-limit → quota_exhausted; 429 → transient; mixed chain ending in quota → quota_exhausted (AC1).
- `UT-2` — park path: label + comment + no status reset (AC2); probe-success un-park (AC3).
- `REG-1` — gh-742 reset-path tests unchanged on transient fixtures (AC4).

## Non-goals

- Provider failover config (the chain already exists and was exhausted — this card governs the aftermath, not provider selection).
- Cross-repo quota accounting.

## References

- Live: fa gh-1697 dev leg, run 39210285663 (2026-10-19 06:33Z), "Provider chain exhausted: 2 of 2"
- gh-742 (interrupted-mid-run reset — correct for transients)

+# Quota Park Probe
+
+Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded probe count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).
+
+Probe success means the quota window has reset or the provider was reconfigured — the handler removes the park label, clears the development/rework dispatch trigger labels, moves the ticket back to Ready For Development and posts an un-park comment, so the normal dispatch lanes resume on the next tick. Probe failure keeps the park and posts a one-line `quota-probe: <n>` marker comment that doubles as the durable counter for the next tick's cadence decision.
+
+## Parameters
+
+- `jobParams.quotaParkLabel` — park label name to watch and remove (default `provider_quota`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = provider_quota`) must be overridden to match.
+- `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` — probe cadence in SM ticks (default 3). The first tick after the park always probes (a misclassification self-corrects immediately).
+- `jobParams.quotaProbeCommand` — the cheap provider ping shell command (default: a 1-token chat completion against the fa provider config `FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` / `FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` / `FA_PROVIDER_MODEL`; curl `--fail` keeps the park on any HTTP error). Override for non-fa provider shapes.
+
+A human un-parks immediately by removing the park label from the ticket — the probe rule stops matching and no further probes fire.

# gh-1087: [GOAL] Quota circuit-breaker: provider-quota exhaustion (403 usage-limit) parks the lane instead of per-tick retry burn (live: fa gh-1697 loop risk)

## Description

## Goal — provider-quota exhaustion parks the leg lane instead of per-tick retry burn (v1)

One sentence: **a hard provider-quota failure (403 weekly/usage-limit, not transient 429) parks the ticket's leg lane with a visible label and a reason comment** — retries resume only after the quota window resets or a human reconfigures the provider — instead of resetting the ticket for an immediate retry that is guaranteed to fail again.

Live: fa gh-1697, 2026-10-19 06:31–06:33Z — z.ai `glm-5.3-flash` answered 403 "weekly (7-day) usage limit" (9 retries), the whole provider chain exhausted, fa exited 1, gh-742 reset the ticket to Ready For Development. The next SM tick re-dispatches the same leg into the same exhausted chain — a burn loop measured in runner-minutes and noise comments until the 7-day window resets.

## Root cause

The interruption classifier treats a quota-exhausted chain the same as a transient interruption (rate limit blip, network cut). Transients deserve immediate retry; a 7-day quota wall does not. The signal is distinguishable: HTTP 403 with a usage-limit body vs 429 rate-limit.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The leg's agent-failure classification distinguishes `quota_exhausted` (403 usage-limit / billing bodies, "Provider chain exhausted" after quota responses) from `transient` (429, timeouts, cuts). Fixture-driven unit test on the classifier.
- **AC2** — On `quota_exhausted`: the ticket is NOT reset to Ready For Development; instead it (and the PR if present) gets a park label (e.g. `provider_quota`) with a comment naming the provider, the quota window text, and the reset condition. The SM excludes the label from dispatch lanes.
- **AC3** — The park self-lifts when a bounded probe (one cheap provider ping per N ticks, not a full leg) succeeds — or a human removes the label. Probe cadence and the label name are config (`jobParams`), defaults sane.
- **AC4** — Transient interruptions keep today's gh-742 behavior exactly (reset + retry) — regression guard.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — classifier: 403-weekly-limit → quota_exhausted; 429 → transient; mixed chain ending in quota → quota_exhausted (AC1).
- `UT-2` — park path: label + comment + no status reset (AC2); probe-success un-park (AC3).
- `REG-1` — gh-742 reset-path tests unchanged on transient fixtures (AC4).

## Non-goals

- Provider failover config (the chain already exists and was exhausted — this card governs the aftermath, not provider selection).
- Cross-repo quota accounting.

## References

- Live: fa gh-1697 dev leg, run 39210285663 (2026-10-19 06:33Z), "Provider chain exhausted: 2 of 2"
- gh-742 (interrupted-mid-run reset — correct for transients)

+# Quota Park Probe
+
+Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded probe count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).
+
+Probe success means the quota window has reset or the provider was reconfigured — the handler removes the park label, clears the development/rework dispatch trigger labels, moves the ticket back to Ready For Development and posts an un-park comment, so the normal dispatch lanes resume on the next tick. Probe failure keeps the park and posts a one-line `quota-probe: <n>` marker comment that doubles as the durable counter for the next tick's cadence decision.
+
+## Parameters
+
+- `jobParams.quotaParkLabel` — park label name to watch and remove (default `provider_quota`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = provider_quota`) must be overridden to match.
+- `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` — probe cadence in SM ticks (default 3). The first tick after the park always probes (a misclassification self-corrects immediately).
+- `jobParams.quotaProbeCommand` — the cheap provider ping shell command (default: a 1-token chat completion against the fa provider config `FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` / `FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` / `FA_PROVIDER_MODEL`; curl `--fail` keeps the park on any HTTP error). Override for non-fa provider shapes.
+
+A human un-parks immediately by removing the park label from the ticket — the probe rule stops matching and no further probes fire.

+/**

# gh-1087: [GOAL] Quota circuit-breaker: provider-quota exhaustion (403 usage-limit) parks the lane instead of per-tick retry burn (live: fa gh-1697 loop risk)

## Description

## Goal — provider-quota exhaustion parks the leg lane instead of per-tick retry burn (v1)

One sentence: **a hard provider-quota failure (403 weekly/usage-limit, not transient 429) parks the ticket's leg lane with a visible label and a reason comment** — retries resume only after the quota window resets or a human reconfigures the provider — instead of resetting the ticket for an immediate retry that is guaranteed to fail again.

Live: fa gh-1697, 2026-10-19 06:31–06:33Z — z.ai `glm-5.3-flash` answered 403 "weekly (7-day) usage limit" (9 retries), the whole provider chain exhausted, fa exited 1, gh-742 reset the ticket to Ready For Development. The next SM tick re-dispatches the same leg into the same exhausted chain — a burn loop measured in runner-minutes and noise comments until the 7-day window resets.

## Root cause

The interruption classifier treats a quota-exhausted chain the same as a transient interruption (rate limit blip, network cut). Transients deserve immediate retry; a 7-day quota wall does not. The signal is distinguishable: HTTP 403 with a usage-limit body vs 429 rate-limit.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The leg's agent-failure classification distinguishes `quota_exhausted` (403 usage-limit / billing bodies, "Provider chain exhausted" after quota responses) from `transient` (429, timeouts, cuts). Fixture-driven unit test on the classifier.
- **AC2** — On `quota_exhausted`: the ticket is NOT reset to Ready For Development; instead it (and the PR if present) gets a park label (e.g. `provider_quota`) with a comment naming the provider, the quota window text, and the reset condition. The SM excludes the label from dispatch lanes.
- **AC3** — The park self-lifts when a bounded probe (one cheap provider ping per N ticks, not a full leg) succeeds — or a human removes the label. Probe cadence and the label name are config (`jobParams`), defaults sane.
- **AC4** — Transient interruptions keep today's gh-742 behavior exactly (reset + retry) — regression guard.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — classifier: 403-weekly-limit → quota_exhausted; 429 → transient; mixed chain ending in quota → quota_exhausted (AC1).
- `UT-2` — park path: label + comment + no status reset (AC2); probe-success un-park (AC3).
- `REG-1` — gh-742 reset-path tests unchanged on transient fixtures (AC4).

## Non-goals

- Provider failover config (the chain already exists and was exhausted — this card governs the aftermath, not provider selection).
- Cross-repo quota accounting.

## References

- Live: fa gh-1697 dev leg, run 39210285663 (2026-10-19 06:33Z), "Provider chain exhausted: 2 of 2"
- gh-742 (interrupted-mid-run reset — correct for transients)

+# Quota Park Probe
+
+Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded probe count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).

+## Parameters

+- `jobParams.quotaParkLabel` — park label name to watch and remove (default `provider_quota`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = provider_quota`) must be overridden to match.

+A human un-parks immediately by removing the park label from the ticket — the probe rule stops matching and no further probes fire.

# gh-1087: [GOAL] Quota circuit-breaker: provider-quota exhaustion (403 usage-limit) parks the lane instead of per-tick retry burn (live: fa gh-1697 loop risk)

## Description

## Goal — provider-quota exhaustion parks the leg lane instead of per-tick retry burn (v1)

One sentence: **a hard provider-quota failure (403 weekly/usage-limit, not transient 429) parks the ticket's leg lane with a visible label and a reason comment** — retries resume only after the quota window resets or a human reconfigures the provider — instead of resetting the ticket for an immediate retry that is guaranteed to fail again.

Live: fa gh-1697, 2026-10-19 06:31–06:33Z — z.ai `glm-5.3-flash` answered 403 "weekly (7-day) usage limit" (9 retries), the whole provider chain exhausted, fa exited 1, gh-742 reset the ticket to Ready For Development. The next SM tick re-dispatches the same leg into the same exhausted chain — a burn loop measured in runner-minutes and noise comments until the 7-day window resets.

## Root cause

The interruption classifier treats a quota-exhausted chain the same as a transient interruption (rate limit blip, network cut). Transients deserve immediate retry; a 7-day quota wall does not. The signal is distinguishable: HTTP 403 with a usage-limit body vs 429 rate-limit.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The leg's agent-failure classification distinguishes `quota_exhausted` (403 usage-limit / billing bodies, "Provider chain exhausted" after quota responses) from `transient` (429, timeouts, cuts). Fixture-driven unit test on the classifier.
- **AC2** — On `quota_exhausted`: the ticket is NOT reset to Ready For Development; instead it (and the PR if present) gets a park label (e.g. `provider_quota`) with a comment naming the provider, the quota window text, and the reset condition. The SM excludes the label from dispatch lanes.
- **AC3** — The park self-lifts when a bounded probe (one cheap provider ping per N ticks, not a full leg) succeeds — or a human removes the label. Probe cadence and the label name are config (`jobParams`), defaults sane.
- **AC4** — Transient interruptions keep today's gh-742 behavior exactly (reset + retry) — regression guard.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — classifier: 403-weekly-limit → quota_exhausted; 429 → transient; mixed chain ending in quota → quota_exhausted (AC1).
- `UT-2` — park path: label + comment + no status reset (AC2); probe-success un-park (AC3).
- `REG-1` — gh-742 reset-path tests unchanged on transient fixtures (AC4).

# gh-1087: [GOAL] Quota circuit-breaker: provider-quota exhaustion (403 usage-limit) parks the lane instead of per-tick retry burn (live: fa gh-1697 loop risk)

## Description

## Goal — provider-quota exhaustion parks the leg lane instead of per-tick retry burn (v1)

One sentence: **a hard provider-quota failure (403 weekly/usage-limit, not transient 429) parks the ticket's leg lane with a visible label and a reason comment** — retries resume only after the quota window resets or a human reconfigures the provider — instead of resetting the ticket for an immediate retry that is guaranteed to fail again.

Live: fa gh-1697, 2026-10-19 06:31–06:33Z — z.ai `glm-5.3-flash` answered 403 "weekly (7-day) usage limit" (9 retries), the whole provider chain exhausted, fa exited 1, gh-742 reset the ticket to Ready For Development. The next SM tick re-dispatches the same leg into the same exhausted chain — a burn loop measured in runner-minutes and noise comments until the 7-day window resets.

## Root cause

The interruption classifier treats a quota-exhausted chain the same as a transient interruption (rate limit blip, network cut). Transients deserve immediate retry; a 7-day quota wall does not. The signal is distinguishable: HTTP 403 with a usage-limit body vs 429 rate-limit.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The leg's agent-failure classification distinguishes `quota_exhausted` (403 usage-limit / billing bodies, "Provider chain exhausted" after quota responses) from `transient` (429, timeouts, cuts). Fixture-driven unit test on the classifier.
- **AC2** — On `quota_exhausted`: the ticket is NOT reset to Ready For Development; instead it (and the PR if present) gets a park label (e.g. `provider_quota`) with a comment naming the provider, the quota window text, and the reset condition. The SM excludes the label from dispatch lanes.
- **AC3** — The park self-lifts when a bounded probe (one cheap provider ping per N ticks, not a full leg) succeeds — or a human removes the label. Probe cadence and the label name are config (`jobParams`), defaults sane.
- **AC4** — Transient interruptions keep today's gh-742 behavior exactly (reset + retry) — regression guard.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — classifier: 403-weekly-limit → quota_exhausted; 429 → transient; mixed chain ending in quota → quota_exhausted (AC1).
- `UT-2` — park path: label + comment + no status reset (AC2); probe-success un-park (AC3).
- `REG-1` — gh-742 reset-path tests unchanged on transient fixtures (AC4).

## Non-goals

- Provider failover config (the chain already exists and was exhausted — this card governs the aftermath, not provider selection).
- Cross-repo quota accounting.

## References

- Live: fa gh-1697 dev leg, run 39210285663 (2026-10-19 06:33Z), "Provider chain exhausted: 2 of 2"
- gh-742 (interrupted-mid-run reset — correct for transients)

+# Quota Park Probe
+
+Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded probe count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).
+
+Probe success means the quota window has reset or the provider was reconfigured — the handler removes the park label, clears the development/rework dispatch trigger labels, moves the ticket back to Ready For Development and posts an un-park comment, so the normal dispatch lanes resume on the next tick. Probe failure keeps the park and posts a one-line `quota-probe: <n>` marker comment that doubles as the durable counter for the next tick's cadence decision.
+
+## Parameters
+
+- `jobParams.quotaParkLabel` — park label name to watch and remove (default `provider_quota`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = provider_quota`) must be overridden to match.
+- `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` — probe cadence in SM ticks (default 3). The first tick after the park always probes (a misclassification self-corrects immediately).
+- `jobParams.quotaProbeCommand` — the cheap provider ping shell command (default: a 1-token chat completion against the fa provider config `FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` / `FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` / `FA_PROVIDER_MODEL`; curl `--fail` keeps the park on any HTTP error). Override for non-fa provider shapes.
+
+A human un-parks immediately by removing the park label from the ticket — the probe rule stops matching and no further probes fire.

# gh-1087: [GOAL] Quota circuit-breaker: provider-quota exhaustion (403 usage-limit) parks the lane instead of per-tick retry burn (live: fa gh-1697 loop risk)

## Description

## Goal — provider-quota exhaustion parks the leg lane instead of per-tick retry burn (v1)

One sentence: **a hard provider-quota failure (403 weekly/usage-limit, not transient 429) parks the ticket's leg lane with a visible label and a reason comment** — retries resume only after the quota window resets or a human reconfigures the provider — instead of resetting the ticket for an immediate retry that is guaranteed to fail again.

Live: fa gh-1697, 2026-10-19 06:31–06:33Z — z.ai `glm-5.3-flash` answered 403 "weekly (7-day) usage limit" (9 retries), the whole provider chain exhausted, fa exited 1, gh-742 reset the ticket to Ready For Development. The next SM tick re-dispatches the same leg into the same exhausted chain — a burn loop measured in runner-minutes and noise comments until the 7-day window resets.

## Root cause

The interruption classifier treats a quota-exhausted chain the same as a transient interruption (rate limit blip, network cut). Transients deserve immediate retry; a 7-day quota wall does not. The signal is distinguishable: HTTP 403 with a usage-limit body vs 429 rate-limit.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The leg's agent-failure classification distinguishes `quota_exhausted` (403 usage-limit / billing bodies, "Provider chain exhausted" after quota responses) from `transient` (429, timeouts, cuts). Fixture-driven unit test on the classifier.
- **AC2** — On `quota_exhausted`: the ticket is NOT reset to Ready For Development; instead it (and the PR if present) gets a park label (e.g. `provider_quota`) with a comment naming the provider, the quota window text, and the reset condition. The SM excludes the label from dispatch lanes.
- **AC3** — The park self-lifts when a bounded probe (one cheap provider ping per N ticks, not a full leg) succeeds — or a human removes the label. Probe cadence and the label name are config (`jobParams`), defaults sane.
- **AC4** — Transient interruptions keep today's gh-742 behavior exactly (reset + retry) — regression guard.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — classifier: 403-weekly-limit → quota_exhausted; 429 → transient; mixed chain ending in quota → quota_exhausted (AC1).
- `UT-2` — park path: label + comment + no status reset (AC2); probe-success un-park (AC3).
- `REG-1` — gh-742 reset-path tests unchanged on transient fixtures (AC4).

## Non-goals

- Provider failover config (the chain already exists and was exhausted — this card governs the aftermath, not provider selection).
- Cross-repo quota accounting.

## References

- Live: fa gh-1697 dev leg, run 39210285663 (2026-10-19 06:33Z), "Provider chain exhausted: 2 of 2"
- gh-742 (interrupted-mid-run reset — correct for transients)

+# Quota Park Probe
+
+Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded probe count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).

# gh-1087: [GOAL] Quota circuit-breaker: provider-quota exhaustion (403 usage-limit) parks the lane instead of per-tick retry burn (live: fa gh-1697 loop risk)

## Description

## Goal — provider-quota exhaustion parks the leg lane instead of per-tick retry burn (v1)

One sentence: **a hard provider-quota failure (403 weekly/usage-limit, not transient 429) parks the ticket's leg lane with a visible label and a reason comment** — retries resume only after the quota window resets or a human reconfigures the provider — instead of resetting the ticket for an immediate retry that is guaranteed to fail again.

Live: fa gh-1697, 2026-10-19 06:31–06:33Z — z.ai `glm-5.3-flash` answered 403 "weekly (7-day) usage limit" (9 retries), the whole provider chain exhausted, fa exited 1, gh-742 reset the ticket to Ready For Development. The next SM tick re-dispatches the same leg into the same exhausted chain — a burn loop measured in runner-minutes and noise comments until the 7-day window resets.

## Root cause

The interruption classifier treats a quota-exhausted chain the same as a transient interruption (rate limit blip, network cut). Transients deserve immediate retry; a 7-day quota wall does not. The signal is distinguishable: HTTP 403 with a usage-limit body vs 429 rate-limit.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The leg's agent-failure classification distinguishes `quota_exhausted` (403 usage-limit / billing bodies, "Provider chain exhausted" after quota responses) from `transient` (429, timeouts, cuts). Fixture-driven unit test on the classifier.
- **AC2** — On `quota_exhausted`: the ticket is NOT reset to Ready For Development; instead it (and the PR if present) gets a park label (e.g. `provider_quota`) with a comment naming the provider, the quota window text, and the reset condition. The SM excludes the label from dispatch lanes.
- **AC3** — The park self-lifts when a bounded probe (one cheap provider ping per N ticks, not a full leg) succeeds — or a human removes the label. Probe cadence and the label name are config (`jobParams`), defaults sane.
- **AC4** — Transient interruptions keep today's gh-742 behavior exactly (reset + retry) — regression guard.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — classifier: 403-weekly-limit → quota_exhausted; 429 → transient; mixed chain ending in quota → quota_exhausted (AC1).
- `UT-2` — park path: label + comment + no status reset (AC2); probe-success un-park (AC3).
- `REG-1` — gh-742 reset-path tests unchanged on transient fixtures (AC4).

## Non-goals

- Provider failover config (the chain already exists and was exhausted — this card governs the aftermath, not provider selection).
- Cross-repo quota accounting.

## References

- Live: fa gh-1697 dev leg, run 39210285663 (2026-10-19 06:33Z), "Provider chain exhausted: 2 of 2"
- gh-742 (interrupted-mid-run reset — correct for transients)

+# Quota Park Probe
+
+Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded probe count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).

# gh-1087: [GOAL] Quota circuit-breaker: provider-quota exhaustion (403 usage-limit) parks the lane instead of per-tick retry burn (live: fa gh-1697 loop risk)

## Description

## Goal — provider-quota exhaustion parks the leg lane instead of per-tick retry burn (v1)

One sentence: **a hard provider-quota failure (403 weekly/usage-limit, not transient 429) parks the ticket's leg lane with a visible label and a reason comment** — retries resume only after the quota window resets or a human reconfigures the provider — instead of resetting the ticket for an immediate retry that is guaranteed to fail again.

Live: fa gh-1697, 2026-10-19 06:31–06:33Z — z.ai `glm-5.3-flash` answered 403 "weekly (7-day) usage limit" (9 retries), the whole provider chain exhausted, fa exited 1, gh-742 reset the ticket to Ready For Development. The next SM tick re-dispatches the same leg into the same exhausted chain — a burn loop measured in runner-minutes and noise comments until the 7-day window resets.

## Root cause

The interruption classifier treats a quota-exhausted chain the same as a transient interruption (rate limit blip, network cut). Transients deserve immediate retry; a 7-day quota wall does not. The signal is distinguishable: HTTP 403 with a usage-limit body vs 429 rate-limit.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The leg's agent-failure classification distinguishes `quota_exhausted` (403 usage-limit / billing bodies, "Provider chain exhausted" after quota responses) from `transient` (429, timeouts, cuts). Fixture-driven unit test on the classifier.
- **AC2** — On `quota_exhausted`: the ticket is NOT reset to Ready For Development; instead it (and the PR if present) gets a park label (e.g. `provider_quota`) with a comment naming the provider, the quota window text, and the reset condition. The SM excludes the label from dispatch lanes.
- **AC3** — The park self-lifts when a bounded probe (one cheap provider ping per N ticks, not a full leg) succeeds — or a human removes the label. Probe cadence and the label name are config (`jobParams`), defaults sane.
- **AC4** — Transient interruptions keep today's gh-742 behavior exactly (reset + retry) — regression guard.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — classifier: 403-weekly-limit → quota_exhausted; 429 → transient; mixed chain ending in quota → quota_exhausted (AC1).
- `UT-2` — park path: label + comment + no status reset (AC2); probe-success un-park (AC3).
- `REG-1` — gh-742 reset-path tests unchanged on transient fixtures (AC4).

## Non-goals

- Provider failover config (the chain already exists and was exhausted — this card governs the aftermath, not provider selection).
- Cross-repo quota accounting.

## References

- Live: fa gh-1697 dev leg, run 39210285663 (2026-10-19 06:33Z), "Provider chain exhausted: 2 of 2"
- gh-742 (interrupted-mid-run reset — correct for transients)

+# Quota Park Probe
+
+Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded probe count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).

# gh-1087: [GOAL] Quota circuit-breaker: provider-quota exhaustion (403 usage-limit) parks the lane instead of per-tick retry burn (live: fa gh-1697 loop risk)

## Description

## Goal — provider-quota exhaustion parks the leg lane instead of per-tick retry burn (v1)

One sentence: **a hard provider-quota failure (403 weekly/usage-limit, not transient 429) parks the ticket's leg lane with a visible label and a reason comment** — retries resume only after the quota window resets or a human reconfigures the provider — instead of resetting the ticket for an immediate retry that is guaranteed to fail again.

Live: fa gh-1697, 2026-10-19 06:31–06:33Z — z.ai `glm-5.3-flash` answered 403 "weekly (7-day) usage limit" (9 retries), the whole provider chain exhausted, fa exited 1, gh-742 reset the ticket to Ready For Development. The next SM tick re-dispatches the same leg into the same exhausted chain — a burn loop measured in runner-minutes and noise comments until the 7-day window resets.

## Root cause

The interruption classifier treats a quota-exhausted chain the same as a transient interruption (rate limit blip, network cut). Transients deserve immediate retry; a 7-day quota wall does not. The signal is distinguishable: HTTP 403 with a usage-limit body vs 429 rate-limit.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The leg's agent-failure classification distinguishes `quota_exhausted` (403 usage-limit / billing bodies, "Provider chain exhausted" after quota responses) from `transient` (429, timeouts, cuts). Fixture-driven unit test on the classifier.
- **AC2** — On `quota_exhausted`: the ticket is NOT reset to Ready For Development; instead it (and the PR if present) gets a park label (e.g. `provider_quota`) with a comment naming the provider, the quota window text, and the reset condition. The SM excludes the label from dispatch lanes.
- **AC3** — The park self-lifts when a bounded probe (one cheap provider ping per N ticks, not a full leg) succeeds — or a human removes the label. Probe cadence and the label name are config (`jobParams`), defaults sane.
- **AC4** — Transient interruptions keep today's gh-742 behavior exactly (reset + retry) — regression guard.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — classifier: 403-weekly-limit → quota_exhausted; 429 → transient; mixed chain ending in quota → quota_exhausted (AC1).
- `UT-2` — park path: label + comment + no status reset (AC2); probe-success un-park (AC3).
- `REG-1` — gh-742 reset-path tests unchanged on transient fixtures (AC4).

## Non-goals

- Provider failover config (the chain already exists and was exhausted — this card governs the aftermath, not provider selection).
- Cross-repo quota accounting.

## References

- Live: fa gh-1697 dev leg, run 39210285663 (2026-10-19 06:33Z), "Provider chain exhausted: 2 of 2"
- gh-742 (interrupted-mid-run reset — correct for transients)

+# Quota Park Probe
+
+Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded probe count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).
+
+Probe success means the quota window has reset or the provider was reconfigured — the handler removes the park label, clears the development/rework dispatch trigger labels, moves the ticket back to Ready For Development and posts an un-park comment, so the normal dispatch lanes resume on the next tick. Probe failure keeps the park and posts a one-line `quota-probe: <n>` marker comment that doubles as the durable counter for the next tick's cadence decision.
+
+## Parameters
+
+- `jobParams.quotaParkLabel` — park label name to watch and remove (default `provider_quota`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = provider_quota`) must be overridden to match.
+- `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` — probe cadence in SM ticks (default 3). The first tick after the park always probes (a misclassification self-corrects immediately).
+- `jobParams.quotaProbeCommand` — the cheap provider ping shell command (default: a 1-token chat completion against the fa provider config `FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` / `FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` / `FA_PROVIDER_MODEL`; curl `--fail` keeps the park on any HTTP error). Override for non-fa provider shapes.
+
+A human un-parks immediately by removing the park label from the ticket — the probe rule stops matching and no further probes fire.

+/**
+ * quotaCircuitBreaker.js — gh-1087 quota circuit-breaker (pure logic, no dmtools globals).
+ *
+ * A hard provider-quota failure (HTTP 403 usage-limit / billing body — e.g.
+ * "weekly (7-day) usage limit" — or a "Provider chain exhausted" tail that
+ * follows quota responses) must PARK the leg lane instead of burning a

+ * the SM dispatch-lane exclusion and the probe cadence are unit-testable
+ * without any tracker/CLI mocks:
+ *
+ *   classifyFailure(text)              → { kind: 'quota_exhausted' | 'transient' | null, ... }
+ *   parkLabelOf(jobParams)             → park label name (default 'provider_quota')
+ *   probeEveryOf(jobParams)            → probe cadence in SM ticks (default 3)
+ *   probeCommandOf(jobParams)          → cheap provider ping shell command
+ *   probeDue(priorCount, everyN)       → is a probe due this tick?
+ *   probeMarkerLine(n)                 → durable per-ticket probe counter line
+ *   countProbeMarkers(bodies)          → probe attempts already recorded

# gh-1087: [GOAL] Quota circuit-breaker: provider-quota exhaustion (403 usage-limit) parks the lane instead of per-tick retry burn (live: fa gh-1697 loop risk)

## Description

## Goal — provider-quota exhaustion parks the leg lane instead of per-tick retry burn (v1)

One sentence: **a hard provider-quota failure (403 weekly/usage-limit, not transient 429) parks the ticket's leg lane with a visible label and a reason comment** — retries resume only after the quota window resets or a human reconfigures the provider — instead of resetting the ticket for an immediate retry that is guaranteed to fail again.

Live: fa gh-1697, 2026-10-19 06:31–06:33Z — z.ai `glm-5.3-flash` answered 403 "weekly (7-day) usage limit" (9 retries), the whole provider chain exhausted, fa exited 1, gh-742 reset the ticket to Ready For Development. The next SM tick re-dispatches the same leg into the same exhausted chain — a burn loop measured in runner-minutes and noise comments until the 7-day window resets.

## Root cause

The interruption classifier treats a quota-exhausted chain the same as a transient interruption (rate limit blip, network cut). Transients deserve immediate retry; a 7-day quota wall does not. The signal is distinguishable: HTTP 403 with a usage-limit body vs 429 rate-limit.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The leg's agent-failure classification distinguishes `quota_exhausted` (403 usage-limit / billing bodies, "Provider chain exhausted" after quota responses) from `transient` (429, timeouts, cuts). Fixture-driven unit test on the classifier.
- **AC2** — On `quota_exhausted`: the ticket is NOT reset to Ready For Development; instead it (and the PR if present) gets a park label (e.g. `provider_quota`) with a comment naming the provider, the quota window text, and the reset condition. The SM excludes the label from dispatch lanes.
- **AC3** — The park self-lifts when a bounded probe (one cheap provider ping per N ticks, not a full leg) succeeds — or a human removes the label. Probe cadence and the label name are config (`jobParams`), defaults sane.
- **AC4** — Transient interruptions keep today's gh-742 behavior exactly (reset + retry) — regression guard.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — classifier: 403-weekly-limit → quota_exhausted; 429 → transient; mixed chain ending in quota → quota_exhausted (AC1).
- `UT-2` — park path: label + comment + no status reset (AC2); probe-success un-park (AC3).
- `REG-1` — gh-742 reset-path tests unchanged on transient fixtures (AC4).

## Non-goals

- Provider failover config (the chain already exists and was exhausted — this card governs the aftermath, not provider selection).
- Cross-repo quota accounting.

## References

- Live: fa gh-1697 dev leg, run 39210285663 (2026-10-19 06:33Z), "Provider chain exhausted: 2 of 2"
- gh-742 (interrupted-mid-run reset — correct for transients)

+# Quota Park Probe
+
+Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded probe count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).
+
+Probe success means the quota window has reset or the provider was reconfigured — the handler removes the park label, clears the development/rework dispatch trigger labels, moves the ticket back to Ready For Development and posts an un-park comment, so the normal dispatch lanes resume on the next tick. Probe failure keeps the park and posts a one-line `quota-probe: <n>` marker comment that doubles as the durable counter for the next tick's cadence decision.
+
+## Parameters
+
+- `jobParams.quotaParkLabel` — park label name to watch and remove (default `provider_quota`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = provider_quota`) must be overridden to match.
+- `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` — probe cadence in SM ticks (default 3). The first tick after the park always probes (a misclassification self-corrects immediately).
+- `jobParams.quotaProbeCommand` — the cheap provider ping shell command (default: a 1-token chat completion against the fa provider config `FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` / `FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` / `FA_PROVIDER_MODEL`; curl `--fail` keeps the park on any HTTP error). Override for non-fa provider shapes.
+
+A human un-parks immediately by removing the park label from the ticket — the probe rule stops matching and no further probes fire.

# gh-1087: [GOAL] Quota circuit-breaker: provider-quota exhaustion (403 usage-limit) parks the lane instead of per-tick retry burn (live: fa gh-1697 loop risk)

## Description

## Goal — provider-quota exhaustion parks the leg lane instead of per-tick retry burn (v1)

One sentence: **a hard provider-quota failure (403 weekly/usage-limit, not transient 429) parks the ticket's leg lane with a visible label and a reason comment** — retries resume only after the quota window resets or a human reconfigures the provider — instead of resetting the ticket for an immediate retry that is guaranteed to fail again.

Live: fa gh-1697, 2026-10-19 06:31–06:33Z — z.ai `glm-5.3-flash` answered 403 "weekly (7-day) usage limit" (9 retries), the whole provider chain exhausted, fa exited 1, gh-742 reset the ticket to Ready For Development. The next SM tick re-dispatches the same leg into the same exhausted chain — a burn loop measured in runner-minutes and noise comments until the 7-day window resets.

## Root cause

The interruption classifier treats a quota-exhausted chain the same as a transient interruption (rate limit blip, network cut). Transients deserve immediate retry; a 7-day quota wall does not. The signal is distinguishable: HTTP 403 with a usage-limit body vs 429 rate-limit.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The leg's agent-failure classification distinguishes `quota_exhausted` (403 usage-limit / billing bodies, "Provider chain exhausted" after quota responses) from `transient` (429, timeouts, cuts). Fixture-driven unit test on the classifier.
- **AC2** — On `quota_exhausted`: the ticket is NOT reset to Ready For Development; instead it (and the PR if present) gets a park label (e.g. `provider_quota`) with a comment naming the provider, the quota window text, and the reset condition. The SM excludes the label from dispatch lanes.
- **AC3** — The park self-lifts when a bounded probe (one cheap provider ping per N ticks, not a full leg) succeeds — or a human removes the label. Probe cadence and the label name are config (`jobParams`), defaults sane.
- **AC4** — Transient interruptions keep today's gh-742 behavior exactly (reset + retry) — regression guard.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — classifier: 403-weekly-limit → quota_exhausted; 429 → transient; mixed chain ending in quota → quota_exhausted (AC1).
- `UT-2` — park path: label + comment + no status reset (AC2); probe-success un-park (AC3).
- `REG-1` — gh-742 reset-path tests unchanged on transient fixtures (AC4).

## Non-goals

- Provider failover config (the chain already exists and was exhausted — this card governs the aftermath, not provider selection).
- Cross-repo quota accounting.

## References

- Live: fa gh-1697 dev leg, run 39210285663 (2026-10-19 06:33Z), "Provider chain exhausted: 2 of 2"
- gh-742 (interrupted-mid-run reset — correct for transients)

+# Quota Park Probe
+
+Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded probe count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).
+
+Probe success means the quota window has reset or the provider was reconfigured — the handler removes the park label, clears the development/rework dispatch trigger labels, moves the ticket back to Ready For Development and posts an un-park comment, so the normal dispatch lanes resume on the next tick. Probe failure keeps the park and posts a one-line `quota-probe: <n>` marker comment that doubles as the durable counter for the next tick's cadence decision.
+
+## Parameters
+
+- `jobParams.quotaParkLabel` — park label name to watch and remove (default `provider_quota`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = provider_quota`) must be overridden to match.
+- `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` — probe cadence in SM ticks (default 3). The first tick after the park always probes (a misclassification self-corrects immediately).
+- `jobParams.quotaProbeCommand` — the cheap provider ping shell command (default: a 1-token chat completion against the fa provider config `FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` / `FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` / `FA_PROVIDER_MODEL`; curl `--fail` keeps the park on any HTTP error). Override for non-fa provider shapes.
+
+A human un-parks immediately by removing the park label from the ticket — the probe rule stops matching and no further probes fire.

+# quota park probe
+
+Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded probe count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).
+
+Probe success means the quota window has reset or the provider was reconfigured — the handler removes the park label, clears the development/rework dispatch trigger labels, moves the ticket back to Ready For Development and posts an un-park comment, so the normal dispatch lanes resume on the next tick. Probe failure keeps the park and posts a one-line `quota-probe: <n>` marker comment that doubles as the durable counter for the next tick's cadence decision.
+
+## Parameters
+
+- `jobParams.quotaParkLabel` — park label name to watch and remove (default `provider_quota`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = provider_quota`) must be overridden to match.
+- `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` — probe cadence in SM ticks (default 3). The first tick after the park always probes (a misclassification self-corrects immediately).
+- `jobParams.quotaProbeCommand` — the cheap provider ping shell command (default: a 1-token chat completion against the fa provider config `FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` / `FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` / `FA_PROVIDER_MODEL`; curl `--fail` keeps the park on any HTTP error). Override for non-fa provider shapes.
+
+A human un-parks immediately by removing the park label from the ticket — the probe rule stops matching and no further probes fire.

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:

callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # gh-1087: [GOAL] Quota circuit-breaker: provider-quota exhaustion (403 usage-limit) parks the lane instead of per-tick retry burn (live: fa gh-1697 loop risk)

## Description

## Goal — provider-quota exhaustion parks the leg lane instead of per-tick retry burn (v1)

One sentence: **a hard provider-quota failure (403 weekly/usage-limit, not transient 429) parks the ticket's leg lane with a visible label and a reason comment** — retries resume only after the quota window resets or a human reconfigures the provider — instead of resetting the ticket for an immediate retry that is guaranteed to fail again.

Live: fa gh-1697, 2026-10-19 06:31–06:33Z — z.ai `glm-5.3-flash` answered 403 "weekly (7-day) usage limit" (9 retries), the whole provider chain exhausted, fa exited 1, gh-742 reset the ticket to Ready For Development. The next SM tick re-dispatches the same leg into the same exhausted chain — a burn loop measured in runner-minutes and noise comments until the 7-day window resets.

## Root cause

The interruption classifier treats a quota-exhausted chain the same as a transient interruption (rate limit blip, network cut). Transients deserve immediate retry; a 7-day quota wall does not. The signal is distinguishable: HTTP 403 with a usage-limit body vs 429 rate-limit.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The leg's agent-failure classification distinguishes `quota_exhausted` (403 usage-limit / billing bodies, "Provider chain exhausted" after quota responses) from `transient` (429, timeouts, cuts). Fixture-driven unit test on the classifier.
- **AC2** — On `quota_exhausted`: the ticket is NOT reset to Ready For Development; instead it (and the PR if present) gets a park label (e.g. `provider_quota`) with a comment naming the provider, the quota window text, and the reset condition. The SM excludes the label from dispatch lanes.
- **AC3** — The park self-lifts when a bounded probe (one cheap provider ping per N ticks, not a full leg) succeeds — or a human removes the label. Probe cadence and the label name are config (`jobParams`), defaults sane.
- **AC4** — Transient interruptions keep today's gh-742 behavior exactly (reset + retry) — regression guard.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — classifier: 403-weekly-limit → quota_exhausted; 429 → transient; mixed chain ending in quota → quota_exhausted (AC1).
- `UT-2` — park path: label + comment + no status reset (AC2); probe-success un-park (AC3).
- `REG-1` — gh-742 reset-path tests unchanged on transient fixtures (AC4).

## Non-goals

- Provider failover config (the chain already exists and was exhausted — this card governs the aftermath, not provider selection).
- Cross-repo quota accounting.

## References

- Live: fa gh-1697 dev leg, run 39210285663 (2026-10-19 06:33Z), "Provider chain exhausted: 2 of 2"
- gh-742 (interrupted-mid-run reset — correct for transients)

# gh-1087: [GOAL] Quota circuit-breaker: provider-quota exhaustion (403 usage-limit) parks the lane instead of per-tick retry burn (live: fa gh-1697 loop risk)

## Description

## Goal — provider-quota exhaustion parks the leg lane instead of per-tick retry burn (v1)

One sentence: **a hard provider-quota failure (403 weekly/usage-limit, not transient 429) parks the ticket's leg lane with a visible label and a reason comment** — retries resume only after the quota window resets or a human reconfigures the provider — instead of resetting the ticket for an immediate retry that is guaranteed to fail again.

Live: fa gh-1697, 2026-10-19 06:31–06:33Z — z.ai `glm-5.3-flash` answered 403 "weekly (7-day) usage limit" (9 retries), the whole provider chain exhausted, fa exited 1, gh-742 reset the ticket to Ready For Development. The next SM tick re-dispatches the same leg into the same exhausted chain — a burn loop measured in runner-minutes and noise comments until the 7-day window resets.

## Root cause

The interruption classifier treats a quota-exhausted chain the same as a transient interruption (rate limit blip, network cut). Transients deserve immediate retry; a 7-day quota wall does not. The signal is distinguishable: HTTP 403 with a usage-limit body vs 429 rate-limit.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The leg's agent-failure classification distinguishes `quota_exhausted` (403 usage-limit / billing bodies, "Provider chain exhausted" after quota responses) from `transient` (429, timeouts, cuts). Fixture-driven unit test on the classifier.
- **AC2** — On `quota_exhausted`: the ticket is NOT reset to Ready For Development; instead it (and the PR if present) gets a park label (e.g. `provider_quota`) with a comment naming the provider, the quota window text, and the reset condition. The SM excludes the label from dispatch lanes.
- **AC3** — The park self-lifts when a bounded probe (one cheap provider ping per N ticks, not a full leg) succeeds — or a human removes the label. Probe cadence and the label name are config (`jobParams`), defaults sane.
- **AC4** — Transient interruptions keep today's gh-742 behavior exactly (reset + retry) — regression guard.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — classifier: 403-weekly-limit → quota_exhausted; 429 → transient; mixed chain ending in quota → quota_exhausted (AC1).
- `UT-2` — park path: label + comment + no status reset (AC2); probe-success un-park (AC3).
- `REG-1` — gh-742 reset-path tests unchanged on transient fixtures (AC4).

## Non-goals

- Provider failover config (the chain already exists and was exhausted — this card governs the aftermath, not provider selection).
- Cross-repo quota accounting.

## References

- Live: fa gh-1697 dev leg, run 39210285663 (2026-10-19 06:33Z), "Provider chain exhausted: 2 of 2"
- gh-742 (interrupted-mid-run reset — correct for transients)

+# Quota Park Probe
+
+Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded probe count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).

# gh-1087: [GOAL] Quota circuit-breaker: provider-quota exhaustion (403 usage-limit) parks the lane instead of per-tick retry burn (live: fa gh-1697 loop risk)

## Description

## Goal — provider-quota exhaustion parks the leg lane instead of per-tick retry burn (v1)

One sentence: **a hard provider-quota failure (403 weekly/usage-limit, not transient 429) parks the ticket's leg lane with a visible label and a reason comment** — retries resume only after the quota window resets or a human reconfigures the provider — instead of resetting the ticket for an immediate retry that is guaranteed to fail again.

Live: fa gh-1697, 2026-10-19 06:31–06:33Z — z.ai `glm-5.3-flash` answered 403 "weekly (7-day) usage limit" (9 retries), the whole provider chain exhausted, fa exited 1, gh-742 reset the ticket to Ready For Development. The next SM tick re-dispatches the same leg into the same exhausted chain — a burn loop measured in runner-minutes and noise comments until the 7-day window resets.

## Root cause

The interruption classifier treats a quota-exhausted chain the same as a transient interruption (rate limit blip, network cut). Transients deserve immediate retry; a 7-day quota wall does not. The signal is distinguishable: HTTP 403 with a usage-limit body vs 429 rate-limit.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The leg's agent-failure classification distinguishes `quota_exhausted` (403 usage-limit / billing bodies, "Provider chain exhausted" after quota responses) from `transient` (429, timeouts, cuts). Fixture-driven unit test on the classifier.
- **AC2** — On `quota_exhausted`: the ticket is NOT reset to Ready For Development; instead it (and the PR if present) gets a park label (e.g. `provider_quota`) with a comment naming the provider, the quota window text, and the reset condition. The SM excludes the label from dispatch lanes.
- **AC3** — The park self-lifts when a bounded probe (one cheap provider ping per N ticks, not a full leg) succeeds — or a human removes the label. Probe cadence and the label name are config (`jobParams`), defaults sane.
- **AC4** — Transient interruptions keep today's gh-742 behavior exactly (reset + retry) — regression guard.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — classifier: 403-weekly-limit → quota_exhausted; 429 → transient; mixed chain ending in quota → quota_exhausted (AC1).
- `UT-2` — park path: label + comment + no status reset (AC2); probe-success un-park (AC3).
- `REG-1` — gh-742 reset-path tests unchanged on transient fixtures (AC4).

## Non-goals

- Provider failover config (the chain already exists and was exhausted — this card governs the aftermath, not provider selection).
- Cross-repo quota accounting.

## References

- Live: fa gh-1697 dev leg, run 39210285663 (2026-10-19 06:33Z), "Provider chain exhausted: 2 of 2"
- gh-742 (interrupted-mid-run reset — correct for transients)

+# Quota Park Probe
+
+Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded probe count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).
+
+Probe success means the quota window has reset or the provider was reconfigured — the handler removes the park label, clears the development/rework dispatch trigger labels, moves the ticket back to Ready For Development and posts an un-park comment, so the normal dispatch lanes resume on the next tick. Probe failure keeps the park and posts a one-line `quota-probe: <n>` marker comment that doubles as the durable counter for the next tick's cadence decision.
+
+## Parameters
+
+- `jobParams.quotaParkLabel` — park label name to watch and remove (default `provider_quota`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = provider_quota`) must be overridden to match.
+- `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` — probe cadence in SM ticks (default 3). The first tick after the park always probes (a misclassification self-corrects immediately).
+- `jobParams.quotaProbeCommand` — the cheap provider ping shell command (default: a 1-token chat completion against the fa provider config `FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` / `FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` / `FA_PROVIDER_MODEL`; curl `--fail` keeps the park on any HTTP error). Override for non-fa provider shapes.
+
+A human un-parks immediately by removing the park label from the ticket — the probe rule stops matching and no further probes fire.

Tests pass (112 across the three files). Note the simulation was run with mocks, but the deadlock simulation with the pure module already proves the composed cadence bug — the test mocks never run two successive ticks through action().

Wait — actually let me double-check the deadlock claim once more carefully, because maybe comments posted by OTHER sources... no, the logic is: priorCount = countProbeMarkers(coments); probe only fires when priorCount % 3 === 0. After first failed probe posts "quota-probe: 1", priorCount = 1 forever (no other code posts markers). 1 % 3 = 1 ≠ 0. Only a successful probe (which unparks) or human un-park can change state. So yes, exactly one probe per park lifetime. The doc/comment "the next probe fires in ~N SM ticks" is false. AC3 says "The park self-lifts when a bounded probe (one cheap provider ping per N ticks...) succeeds" — with this bug, a quota window that resets after the first failed probe is never detected. The ticket stays parked for up to 7 days until human intervention. That's the whole point of the feature partially defeated. BLOCKING.

The correct fix suggestion: the cadence decision needs a per-tick counter, not a per-probe counter. E.g., post a lightweight `quota-park-tick: n` marker every tick and probe when `n % everyN === 0` (with n starting at 1), or track the last probe comment timestamp vs SM tick interval.

Now other findings:

2. CI "crap" check failed → BLOCKING per rules (F7). Root cause unknown (log fetch failed), likely CRAP complexity regression from new high-branch functions (quotaParkProbe.action, completeInterruptedPath, parkQuotaExhaustedDevelopment). Can't verify locally.

  - `probeDue` modulo semantics: also, if comment posting of the marker fails (caught warn), next tick priorCount stays 0 → probe re-fires every tick until posting succeeds — a silent every-tick burn, the exact thing gh-1087 tries to avoid. Consider this part of the cadence finding.

Log leakage of the *variable name* only, not the value. OK.

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:

callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # gh-1087: [GOAL] Quota circuit-breaker: provider-quota exhaustion (403 usage-limit) parks the lane instead of per-tick retry burn (live: fa gh-1697 loop risk)

## Description

## Goal — provider-quota exhaustion parks the leg lane instead of per-tick retry burn (v1)

One sentence: **a hard provider-quota failure (403 weekly/usage-limit, not transient 429) parks the ticket's leg lane with a visible label and a reason comment** — retries resume only after the quota window resets or a human reconfigures the provider — instead of resetting the ticket for an immediate retry that is guaranteed to fail again.

Live: fa gh-1697, 2026-10-19 06:31–06:33Z — z.ai `glm-5.3-flash` answered 403 "weekly (7-day) usage limit" (9 retries), the whole provider chain exhausted, fa exited 1, gh-742 reset the ticket to Ready For Development. The next SM tick re-dispatches the same leg into the same exhausted chain — a burn loop measured in runner-minutes and noise comments until the 7-day window resets.

## Root cause

The interruption classifier treats a quota-exhausted chain the same as a transient interruption (rate limit blip, network cut). Transients deserve immediate retry; a 7-day quota wall does not. The signal is distinguishable: HTTP 403 with a usage-limit body vs 429 rate-limit.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The leg's agent-failure classification distinguishes `quota_exhausted` (403 usage-limit / billing bodies, "Provider chain exhausted" after quota responses) from `transient` (429, timeouts, cuts). Fixture-driven unit test on the classifier.
- **AC2** — On `quota_exhausted`: the ticket is NOT reset to Ready For Development; instead it (and the PR if present) gets a park label (e.g. `provider_quota`) with a comment naming the provider, the quota window text, and the reset condition. The SM excludes the label from dispatch lanes.
- **AC3** — The park self-lifts when a bounded probe (one cheap provider ping per N ticks, not a full leg) succeeds — or a human removes the label. Probe cadence and the label name are config (`jobParams`), defaults sane.
- **AC4** — Transient interruptions keep today's gh-742 behavior exactly (reset + retry) — regression guard.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — classifier: 403-weekly-limit → quota_exhausted; 429 → transient; mixed chain ending in quota → quota_exhausted (AC1).
- `UT-2` — park path: label + comment + no status reset (AC2); probe-success un-park (AC3).
- `REG-1` — gh-742 reset-path tests unchanged on transient fixtures (AC4).

## Non-goals

- Provider failover config (the chain already exists and was exhausted — this card governs the aftermath, not provider selection).
- Cross-repo quota accounting.

## References

- Live: fa gh-1697 dev leg, run 39210285663 (2026-10-19 06:33Z), "Provider chain exhausted: 2 of 2"
- gh-742 (interrupted-mid-run reset — correct for transients)

+# Quota Park Probe
+
+Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded probe count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).

+
+## Parameters
+
+- `jobParams.quotaParkLabel` — park label name to watch and remove (default `provider_quota`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = provider_quota`) must be overridden to match.
